summary: Core search engine for querying elements within a Revit document.
best_practices: Always chain Quick Filters (OfCategory, OfClass) before Slow Filters. Use WhereElementIsNotElementType() to exclude family symbols. For view-specific queries, pass view.Id: FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).
common_pitfalls: Avoid iterating over whole document when a view collector is sufficient. ToElements() instantiates Python lists; for large sets prefer lazy iteration directly over the collector.

summary: Context for modifying document state. Required for creating, deleting, or altering elements.
syntax_pattern:
from pyrevit import revit
with revit.Transaction('Action Name'):
    element.LookupParameter('Comments').Set('Updated')
best_practices: In pyRevit, wrap operations inside with revit.Transaction('Name'): block. Keep transactions as short and scoped as possible.
common_pitfalls: Starting a transaction during read-only events causes InvalidOperationException. Forgetting to commit or roll back unhandled exceptions can lock Revit.

summary: Specialized 2D views that do not display 3D model geometry.
best_practices: Filter out ViewDrafting elements where view.IsTemplate is True before evaluating element counts. Use FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).GetElementCount() for fast zero-element checks.
common_pitfalls: Attempting to query 3D elements inside drafting views yields empty sets. Deleting an active view causes UI crashes.

summary: Collects user-created and standard worksets in workshared models.
best_practices: Always verify doc.IsWorkshared before instantiating FilteredWorksetCollector. Handle non-workshared models gracefully.
common_pitfalls: Modifying worksets requires active central file connectivity. Attempting workset actions on standard non-workshared .rvt files raises InvalidOperationException.

summary: Element data holder. Access via BuiltInParameter or name lookup.
best_practices: Prefer get_Parameter(BuiltInParameter) over LookupParameter(str) for performance and language independence. Check param.IsReadOnly before Set().
common_pitfalls: LookupParameter returns None if parameter does not exist; calling .Set() directly causes AttributeError.
